endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: This requires completing and documenting a workflow integration assessment, which includes accounting for how the AI solution will affect flow of people and tasks in both physical and digital environments.

endorsements.title: Adoption of AI in Healthcare Delivery Systems: Early Applications and Impacts
endorsements.quote: Health system leaders see clinician burnout as a central challenge to address, which means that productivity or efficiency cannot come at the expense of workforce well-being.

endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: physicians will need to be diligent in ensuring that they engage with AI tools where performance has been validated in their practice setting.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: This includes examining how the AI solution impacts and aligns with organization culture, value, patient needs, and financial incentives.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Assess AI tool’s integration within local clinical workflows | AI tool’s interface aligns with hospital IT system148 or disrupts routine practice

endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement
endorsements.issuer: ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA; Radiol Artif Intell 2024 (PMID 38251899, doi:10.1148/ryai.230513)
endorsements.quote: New products should improve the quality or efficiency of existing workflows in terms of lesion detection, segmentation, diagnosis, or prediction of clinical outcomes.

endorsements.title: Clinical problem selection for machine learning-based clinical decision support in the intensive care unit: complexity, actionability, and the way forward
endorsements.quote: Though the elements of the checklist have empirical basis, multidisciplinary discussion is required to decide whether to pursue the candidate problem through the lens of actionability.

endorsements.title: Artificial intelligence and nursing science: Opportunities, challenges, implications, and guidelines
endorsements.quote: Nurse scientist–led financial evaluation further differs from generic AI integration efforts by explicitly modeling costs and benefits at the level of nursing work, including time-on-task, staffing mix, surveillance burden, moral distress, training load, and impacts on care continuity—dimensions that are rarely captured in institutional ROI calculations.

endorsements.title: Governing the attention dividend: AI-reclaimed clinician capacity as a health policy resource
endorsements.quote: Workforce impact assessment before and after deployment; staffing adjustments funded before throughput expansion

endorsements.title: Human-centered digital ecosystem: safeguarding healthcare workers' sleep, ergonomics, and occupational health
endorsements.quote: Consequently, institutions must proactively ensure that time saved is genuinely converted into protected recovery or direct patient care, rather than being backfilled with additional administrative duties or patient appointments.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Should Not Prescribe Alone: A Risk-Stratified Pharmacy Governance Framework for Agentic Clinical Systems
endorsements.quote: Institutions should assess this workload before implementation and provide staffing, training and decision-making authority proportionate to the risk of the task.

evidence.title: Transforming Non-Digital, Clinical Workflows to Detect and Track Vision-Threatening Diabetic Retinopathy via a Digital Platform Integrating Artificial Intelligence: Implementation Research
evidence.outcome: Duration of screening workflow
evidence.effect: The median screening duration per patient was 6:30 minutes for AI compared to 5:38 minutes for manual screening.
evidence.quote: The median duration for a patient in the AI and manual screening was 6:30 and 5:38 min, respectively.

evidence.title: A Pragmatic Randomized Trial of an EHR-Integrated Generative AI Chart Summarization Tool for Ambulatory Clinicians
evidence.outcome: Physician task load (PTL) and burnout in intervention vs control clinicians
evidence.effect: PTL was lower in the intervention arm (−27.4; 95% CI −49.4 to −5.3; P=0.02) and burnout was lower (−0.20); charting time showed no significant difference (−1.2 seconds).
evidence.quote: The adjusted between-arm difference in PTL at follow-up favored the intervention arm (scale 0-400; −27.4; 95% CI, −49.4 to −5.3; P=0.02).

evidence.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of a clinical decision support system (AI-Antidelirium) to improve Nurses' adherence to delirium guidelines in the intensive care unit
evidence.outcome: Nurses' extraneous and germane cognitive load with versus without the AI decision support tool
evidence.effect: AI-AntiDelirium significantly decreased extraneous cognitive load (P < 0.01) and improved germane cognitive load (P < 0.01) versus control units.
evidence.quote: When compared to control groups, AI-AntiDelirium was found to be significantly effective in both decreasing extraneous cognitive load (P < 0.01) and improving germane cognitive load (P < 0.01).

evidence.title: Triaging mammography with artificial intelligence: an implementation study
evidence.outcome: Staff capacity to provide immediate interpretation and same-visit diagnostic imaging
evidence.effect: Radiologists were unavailable within 30 minutes for 6% (8/131) of prioritized cases; 15% (5/33) needing additional imaging were not offered same-visit imaging for operational reasons.
evidence.quote: For 6% (8/131) of AI-prioritized cases, a radiologist was not available to perform an interpretation within 30 minutes; these participants obtained their final screening results by letter as usual (all had negative or benign findings).

evidence.title: An LLM chatbot to facilitate primary-to-specialist care transitions: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: Specialist consultation duration
evidence.effect: Consultation duration: PreA-only 3.14 ± 2.25 versus No-PreA 4.41 ± 2.77 min; P < 0.001; 28.7% (95% CI 22.7–34.8) relative reduction.
evidence.quote: The PreA-only group had a significantly shorter consultation duration compared to the No-PreA group (PreA-only 3.14 ± 2.25 versus No-PreA 4.41 ± 2.77 min; P < 0.001; Fig. 2a ), corresponding to a 28.7% (95% CI 22.7–34.8) relative reduction.

evidence.title: AI at the bedside: Randomised controlled trial of ChatGPT's impact on student performance in real-patient clinical exams
evidence.outcome: Student-reported distraction during bedside assessment
evidence.effect: 37% reported distraction, although 85% found ChatGPT helpful overall.
evidence.quote: Participants in the intervention arm found ChatGPT helpful overall (85%), particularly for differential diagnosis (92%) and management planning (81%), but performance gains were inconsistent; 37% reported distraction.

evidence.title: AI-Generated Responses to Patient's Messages: Effectiveness, Feasibility and Implementation
evidence.outcome: Review and drafting time with vs without AI drafts; perceived clinical efficiency
evidence.effect: Review and drafting times were similar for users with and without Art; perceived clinical efficiency declined significantly PRE to POST-2; well-being unchanged.
evidence.quote: Review and drafting times were similar for users with and without Art, indicating minimal differences.

evidence.title: Performance and attitudes toward real-time computer-aided polyp detection during colonoscopy in a large tertiary referral center in the United States
evidence.outcome: Staff and endoscopist concerns about false positives, distraction and procedure time after CADe deployment
evidence.effect: Main concerns were false-positive signals (82.4%), high level of distraction (58.8%), and impression it prolonged procedure time (47.1%).
evidence.quote: Survey results demonstrated mixed attitudes toward AI-assisted colonoscopy, of which main concerns were high number of false-positive signals (82.4%), high level of distraction (58.8%), and impression it prolonged procedure time (47.1%).

evidence.title: Deep Learning to Detect Intracranial Hemorrhage in a National Teleradiology Program and the Impact on Interpretation Time
evidence.outcome: Radiologist read times for AI-flagged false positive exams versus baseline
evidence.effect: False-flagged no-bleed exams averaged 9 min 40 s (median 8:07) vs 8 min 25 s pre-AI (n=49,007) and 8:38 for unflagged post-AI (n=52,281), P<.001.
evidence.quote: Of the 56 745 post-AI CT scans with no bleed identified by a radiologist, examinations falsely flagged as suspected ICH by the AI solution (n = 4464) took an average of 9 minutes 40 seconds (median, 8 minutes 7 seconds) to interpret as compared with 8 minutes 25 seconds (median, 6 minutes 48 seconds) for unremarkable CT scans before AI (n = 49 007) (P < .001) and 8 minutes 38 seconds (median, 6 minutes 53 seconds) after AI when ICH was not suspected by the AI solution (n = 52 281) (P < .001).

evidence.title: Transforming Non-Digital, Clinical Workflows to Detect and Track Vision-Threatening Diabetic Retinopathy via a Digital Platform Integrating Artificial Intelligence: Implementation Research
evidence.outcome: Median screening workflow duration per patient
evidence.effect: Median screening duration was 6:30 min with AI versus 5:38 min with manual screening, excluding patient registration.
evidence.quote: The median duration for a patient in the AI and manual screening was 6:30 and 5:38 min, respectively.

evidence.title: Measuring the Impact of AI on Report-Drafting Efficiency in Chest Computed Tomography Interpretation: Retrospective Analysis
evidence.outcome: Change in radiologist report-drafting time after AI lung nodule deployment, by hospital
evidence.effect: Pooled increase of 0.86 min (95% CI 0.14 to 1.57). Tsinghua Changgung: nonsignificant +0.90 min. Beijing Anzhen: reductions of 0.76 min at year 1 and a further 1.83 min at year 2 (about 28% time saved).
evidence.quote: AI-assisted lung nodule diagnosis may initially increase report-drafting time due to adaptation and workflow adjustment.

evidence.title: Prospective evaluation of a large language model clinical decision support system in the emergency department
evidence.outcome: Clinician adoption of AI tool over time and relation to workload
evidence.effect: Adoption declined from 68% to 30%, with workload-sensitive disengagement (OR = 0.72 per shift hour, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.83).
evidence.quote: Clinical adoption of SHAKED declined from 68% to 30%, owing to workload-sensitive disengagement (OR = 0.72 per shift hour, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.83).

evidence.title: Evaluation of a Large Language Model Discharge Summary Hospital Course Tool: Improved Quality but Longer Documentation Time
evidence.outcome: Discharge summary edit time before and after AI hospital course tool, and by tool use
evidence.effect: No overall change between periods (6.60 vs 6.28 min, p=0.11); edit time longer with AI use (9.20 vs 4.93 min, p<0.001); adjusted 32% increase (95% CI 24%-41%).
evidence.quote: Among 2,206 encounters in the Post-AI period, edit time was longer when the AI tool was used (9.20 [IQR 4.9-16.3] vs 4.93 [IQR 2.5-9.7] minutes, p<0.001).

evidence.title: Utilization of Generative AI-drafted Responses for Managing Patient-Provider Communication
evidence.outcome: Unnecessary draft generation and clinician review burden
evidence.effect: GenAI drafts were generated for all messages, including 80% that received no response, adding to review burden.
evidence.quote: GenAI drafts were generated for all messages, including 80% that received no response, adding to the review burden and potentially undermining efficiency.

evidence.title: Clinical Implementation of a Combined Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing Quality Assurance Program for Pulmonary Nodule Detection in the Emergency Department Setting
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: Effect of background AI-NLP quality assurance on radiologist workflow and follow-up delays
evidence.effect: Of 19,246 CTs, 50 (0.26%) went to secondary review; 34 of 50 (68%) led to addenda; median time to addendum was 11 hours; no workflow disruption reported.
evidence.quote: This was achieved without disrupting in-shift radiologist workflow or causing significant delays in patient follow for the diagnosed pulmonary nodule.

evidence.title: The incremental design of a machine learning framework for medical records processing
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Individual fax-processing time
evidence.effect: Mean processing time decreased by 147.5 s; event-log analysis of over 7000 faxes reinforced this finding.
evidence.quote: Our observation analysis showed a mean reduction in individual fax processing time by 147.5 s, while our event log analysis of over 7000 faxes reinforced this finding.

evidence.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Insertable Cardiac Monitors on Device Clinic Workflow and Resource Utilization
evidence.outcome: Nonactionable alert volume, staffing hours and costs, AI-enhanced vs non-AI ICMs per 600-patient clinic
evidence.effect: NAAs 5,078 (non-AI) vs 2,110 (AI-enhanced) annually; 559 fewer staffing hours (956 vs 397; P<0.001); $29,470 annual savings.
evidence.quote: The mean annual NAA volume per 600-ICM clinic was 5,078 for non-AI-enhanced ICMs and 2,110 for AI-enhanced ICMs, resulting in 559 fewer staffing hours (956 vs 397 hours; 95% CI: 513-605 hours; P value < 0.001) and $29,470 in annual savings ($20,929 vs $50,399; 95% CI: $27,035-$31,904; P value < 0.001).

evidence.title: Increasing Advance Care Planning Discussions and Documentation
evidence.venue: Journal of the advanced practitioner in oncology
evidence.outcome: Provider-perceived workflow disruption from AI-triggered ACP notifications
evidence.effect: 83.3% of 12 survey respondents (55% response rate) reported the notification and ACP implementation was not disruptive to workflow.
evidence.quote: When asked whether the ACP implementation was disruptive to workflow, 83.3% of respondents reported it was not.

evidence.title: Mixed-methods evaluation of how a predictive model pilot intervention addresses patient non-attendance at outpatient services in an NHS Foundation Trust in England
evidence.outcome: Team capacity and prioritisation to act on predictive model outputs
evidence.effect: Differing prioritisation of the intervention amid long waiting lists and staff resourcing issues limited pilot success; only 3 of 9 services significantly reduced non-attendance in phase 1, and 1 in phase 2 (20.4% to 19.1%, p<0.05).
evidence.quote: Differing perceptions of how the intervention should be prioritised, especially in the context of long waiting lists and staff resourcing issues, offer some context to the limits of the pilot's success.

evidence.title: Physicians' perceptions of how digital-intelligent medical technology reshapes job characteristics: a qualitative study
evidence.outcome: Physician-perceived job demands, burnout and efficiency effects of AI tools
evidence.effect: Technologies were perceived to improve efficiency and decision accuracy, but also added operational complexity and burnout risk; qualitative only, no quantified effects.
evidence.quote: Challenges such as technical dependency, operational complexity, and ethical responsibility arising from digital-intelligent medical technologies impose new job demands on physicians, exacerbating burnout and skill degradation risks.

evidence.title: Assessing Artificial Intelligence in Breast Imaging: A Survey of Breast Radiologists' Insights on Adoption, Benefits, and Challenges
evidence.outcome: Radiologist-reported AI impact on workflow efficiency, burnout, and turnaround time
evidence.effect: Respondents reported great impacts on workflow efficiency (109, 73.2%), reducing burnout (70, 47.0%), and turnaround time (70, 47.0%); integration was a barrier (98, 62.0%).
evidence.quote: Additionally, respondents reported AI tools have great impacts on workflow efficiency (109, 73.2%), patient care (98, 65.8%), reducing burnout (70, 47.0%), turnaround time (70, 47.0%), and addressing radiologist shortages (69, 46.3%).

evidence.title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm to Increase Productivity in Implantable Loop Recorder Monitoring: A Multicentre Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Clinician-facing alert burden and estimated physiologist review workload
evidence.effect: Clinician-facing alerts decreased from 4,261 to 2,509 (41.1%). Suppression of 1,007 alerts corresponded to estimated savings of 185-218 hours annually (3.6-4.2 hours per week); review time was not directly measured.
evidence.quote: Applying published time-and-motion estimates for remote transmission review (11-13 minutes per alert), suppression of 1,007 alerts by the AI algorithm was estimated to release approximately 185-218 hours of physiologist review time annually, equivalent to 3.6-4.2 hours per week of re-deployable service capacity.

evidence.title: Radiologist Perceptions of an AI Tool for Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection in Teleradiology: Cross-Sectional Survey Study
evidence.outcome: Perceived false-positive burden and time savings from AI in radiology workflow
evidence.effect: Only 10.8% (7/65) reported reduced overall interpretation time; 33.8% (22/65) agreed false-positive review time outweighed benefits; 18.5% found false-positive alerts acceptably infrequent.
evidence.quote: Only 10.8% (7/65; 95% CI 5.3%-20.6%) reported reduced overall interpretation time, whereas 33.8% (22/65; 95% CI 23.5%-46.0%) agreed that time spent reviewing false-positive alerts outweighed the benefits.

evidence.title: Multisite Implementation of a Digital Wound Model of Care: A Post-Implementation Multimethods Evaluation of Patient and Clinician Perspectives and Lessons Learned
evidence.outcome: Clinician-reported barriers to workflow integration of the AI wound app, including time and training burden
evidence.effect: Frontline clinicians valued enhanced documentation consistency but reported barriers including time pressures and training burden; workflow integration was flagged as a priority area for future investment.
evidence.quote: Frontline clinicians valued enhanced documentation consistency but reported barriers including time pressures and training burden.
evidence.sample_unit: participants (patients, frontline clinicians, senior wound nurses, product manager)

evidence.title: Usability and Workflow Integration of a Machine Learning-Derived Neonatal Risk Predictor in Kenyan Neonatal Units: Multisite User-Centered Pilot Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Reported documentation burden and workflow integration after ML risk tool implementation
evidence.effect: 40% (4/10) reported increased documentation burden during high patient volume; 80% (8/10) agreed the tool improves care prioritization within 48 hours.
evidence.quote: However, workflow integration was workload-sensitive: 40% (4/10) reported an increased documentation burden during periods of high patient volume.
evidence.sample_unit: frontline neonatal health care workers (plus 3 key informant interviewees)

evidence.title: Evaluating an LLM-Assisted Workflow for Clinical Documentation:  A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial on Time and Quality
evidence.outcome: document creation time
evidence.effect: Summaries were shorter with clinician-in-loop (β = −59.4 seconds; 95% CI, −118.1 to −0.8; P = .047), but referrals took longer (β = 94.8 seconds; 95% CI, 40.4 to 149.3; P<.001).
evidence.quote: For referrals, clinician-in-the-loop required more time (β = 94.8 seconds; 95% CI, 40.4 to 149.3; P<.001).

evidence.title: Towards human-AI collaboration in radiology: a multidimensional evaluation of the acceptability of AI for chest radiograph analysis in supporting pulmonary tuberculosis diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Radiologist-reported workflow disruption and workload burden with AI
evidence.effect: Radiologists reported high satisfaction, minimal workflow disruption, and limited increases in workload burden.
evidence.quote: Radiologists reported high satisfaction with using qXR based on minimal workflow disruptions, respect for their professional autonomy, and limited increases in workload burden despite poor algorithm explainability.

evidence.title: Integrating AI into Clinical Workflows: A Simulation Study on Implementing AI-aided Same-day Diagnostic Testing Following an Abnormal Screening Mammogram
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.outcome: workflow disruption and daily patient volume
evidence.effect: minimal disruption (4% volume reduction or 2% operating time increase) under specific conditions
evidence.quote: Using discrete simulation, we found minimal disruption to the workflow (a 4% reduction in daily patient volume or a 2% increase in operating time) under specific conditions: operation from 9 am to 12 pm with all radiologists managing all patient types (screenings, diagnostics, and biopsies).

evidence.title: Optimizing AI implementation for surgery: recommendations for infrastructure and deployment in the operating room
evidence.outcome: Physical workload and frustration associated with AI deployment configurations
evidence.effect: Cloud versus Edge mean differences were 17.33 for physical workload (SD = 14.38, p value = 0.0004) and 14.33 for frustration (SD = 15.91, p value = 0.0036).
evidence.quote: Significant mean differences between Cloud and Edge were found in the “physical” (mean difference = 17.33, SD = 14.38, paired t -test, t (14) = 4.670, p value = 0.0004) and “frustration” subcategories (mean difference = 14.33, SD = 15.91, paired t -test, t (14) = 3.489, p value = 0.0036).

evidence.title: Sequencing AI Automation and Data Interoperability in Oncology Using a Scenario-Planning Framework Coupled With Discrete-Event Simulation: Proof-of-Concept Study
evidence.outcome: Governance/administrative burden and throughput when AI automation lacks interoperability (simulated)
evidence.effect: Automation islands (high A, low I) raised RTTI 26% to 37.1 days and cut throughput to 647 patients/year as governance became the bottleneck.
evidence.quote: In the automation islands scenario ( S II ), we observed the worst system performance, with mean RTTI increasing to 37.1 days, a 26% increase compared to the analog baseline, whereas throughput decreased to 647 patients per year.
evidence.sample_unit: stochastic simulation replications per scenario coordinate

commentary.bottom_line: Eleven frameworks and guidance documents endorse assessing workflow, burden, and team capacity before deploying AI, but only one observational study from Thailand measured workflow change, finding that AI screening took a median 6:30 minutes per patient versus 5:38 minutes for manual screening. Hazard studies show that AI can add or reduce clinician burden depending on setting, which suggests local assessment may be useful, though no study shows that conducting the assessment improves outcomes.

perspectives.view: One prospective study with a comparator (n=1375) measured screening time with and without AI in a real deployment. It measured workflow change rather than testing whether a documented assessment prevents burden, so the evidence is indirect. A single observational study without replication supports a rating of very low certainty.

In one trial, radiologists were unavailable within 30 minutes for 6% of AI-prioritized cases, and 15% of patients needing more imaging were not offered it at the same visit for operational reasons. False-flagged head CTs took longer to read. These studies show that capacity gaps exist, but none tests whether prior assessment closes them.

Burden effects vary by site and tool. Two trials found lower task load and cognitive load, while discharge summary edit time rose 32% with AI use and adoption fell from 68% to 30% as shift hours increased. Report time rose a pooled 0.86 minutes across two hospitals whose results diverged. This variation may argue for local measurement.

An AI-enhanced cardiac monitoring program reported 559 fewer staffing hours and $29,470 in annual savings per 600-patient clinic. A predictive no-show model reduced non-attendance in only 3 of 9 services amid long waiting lists and staffing shortfalls. These descriptive studies suggest staffing capacity shapes returns, but none reports what the assessment itself costs.

The one study testing the practice, from Thailand, did not report Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy subgroups. A Chinese trial that included low-income, rural, low-literacy, and non-English-speaking patients found consultations 28.7% shorter with AI pre-assessment, but that trial addresses the hazard rather than the assessment practice.

Endorsement comes from voluntary frameworks, professional guidance, and commentaries. The CHAI Assurance Standards Guide and two guidance documents rate the practice as must. None of the supplied sources cites a federal or state legal requirement for workflow or burden assessment.

In one health system, AI drafts were generated for every patient message, including 80% that received no response, which added review work. In a small trial, 37% of students reported distraction at the bedside when using ChatGPT. Burden that pulls attention from patients may affect trust, but no study measured patient outcomes of a workflow assessment.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares deployments that conducted and documented a workflow and capacity assessment with deployments that did not. A prospective multisite comparison would address this gap if it measured clinician time, response to AI outputs, patient follow-through, and the staffing cost of the assessment, and if it included safety-net settings.
commentary.underserved_note: The only study testing the practice was conducted in Thailand and did not report Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Two hazard studies included limited English proficiency or low-literacy patients (pmid:41555035, epmc:PPR1268213), but neither tested the assessment practice. Organizations serving these groups therefore have no direct evidence on whether assessment helps them.
